rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate all six peaks and identify critical pairs while limiting the late-elution penalty. The low starting organic fraction preserves early retention, and the high endpoint reduces the risk of missing strongly retained compounds.

Injection 1 already achieves the maximum possible CRF. Shorten the gradient by one grid step to test whether full resolution can be retained with earlier elution, keeping injection 1 as the proven optimum.

The shorter gradient preserves maximum CRF but leaves the critical pair close to the resolution threshold. Raise temperature by one step at the same slope to test whether selectivity permits faster elution without losing full resolution.
Test the next shorter gradient at the temperature that improved the critical pair. This establishes the slope limit for full resolution while injection 3 remains a maximum-CRF fallback.

Narrow the organic window to restore approximately the successful 8-minute gradient slope while reducing time spent before the first peak. The endpoint remains well above the estimated last-peak elution composition, limiting the risk of delayed elution.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to reduce initial retention while slightly flattening the gradient to protect the critical pair. This tests a shorter fully resolved run against injection 5, which already achieves maximum CRF.

Shift the start upward to shorten early retention while lowering the endpoint to give the critical pair a shallower gradient. Monitor the first pair for compression; the endpoint remains comfortably above the last peak’s estimated elution composition.

Raise temperature one step to seek earlier final elution without increasing the starting organic fraction, since the first peak is already near the dead time. Monitor both the first pair and the marginal middle pair for temperature-driven selectivity changes.

Trim the endpoint and shorten the gradient to four minutes, giving a slightly steeper slope than injection 8 while retaining headroom above the last peak’s elution composition. This tests a modest time reduction with minimal disturbance to the two limiting pairs.

Test whether a much steeper gradient can carry the slope-sensitive middle pair through an elution-order reversal and restore separation at shorter retention times. The lower starting organic fraction and temperature protect early-pair retention and selectivity; injection 9 remains the fastest proven maximum-CRF method.

Return to the fully resolved regime and test a slope just steeper than injection 9 to locate the fastest full-resolution boundary. The aggressive two-minute gradient did not adequately separate the middle pair, so injection 9 remains the proven fallback.

Test whether higher temperature improves the middle pair enough to support a steeper gradient than injection 9. Lower the starting organic fraction to counter the early-pair compression seen as temperature rises.

Return to 50 C to recover early-pair selectivity and test an intermediate slope with the lower starting organic fraction. This may retain full middle-pair resolution while eluting the last peak sooner than injection 9.

Explore a cooler, high-starting-organic method to test a different selectivity regime for the unresolved pair in the steep gradient. Lower temperature should help retain the early compounds, while the two-minute gradient targets a substantially shorter run; injection 9 remains the fastest proven fully resolved method.

Lower the starting organic fraction to improve the early-pair separation that limited injection 12, while increasing slope to exploit its middle-pair resolution margin. This tests whether 55 C can deliver full resolution near the shortest proven run time.

Test a higher starting organic fraction with a cooler, shallower gradient to preserve early-pair separation and assess middle-pair selectivity. This explores another route to shortening the fully resolved run, with injection 9 retained as the fastest proven maximum-CRF method.

Slightly flatten the slope relative to injection 13 to recover the middle pair’s small resolution deficit while retaining stronger early-pair separation than injection 9. This targets another maximum-CRF method with a last-peak time close to the fastest proven result.

Test one temperature step below the fastest proven fully resolved method to strengthen early-pair separation and measure the middle pair’s temperature margin. Maximum CRF is already secured; this run assesses whether the compact four-minute method remains fully resolved at a cooler setting.

Slightly flatten injection 17’s gradient to increase the middle-pair resolution margin while preserving its stronger early-pair separation. This targets a more robust maximum-CRF method with only a small increase in elution time.

This matches injection 9’s successful slope and starting composition while extending the gradient to a stronger endpoint. It should preserve maximum CRF and the approximately 3.4-minute last-peak time, while testing whether a higher endpoint affects the observed separation.

Lower injection 9’s endpoint by one step to flatten the gradient and increase the critical middle-pair resolution margin. This targets a compact maximum-CRF method with more tolerance to small selectivity changes, accepting slightly later elution.

Lower temperature one step from injection 21 to improve the limiting early pair, using the shallower gradient’s middle-pair resolution margin. This targets a better-balanced fully resolved method, while injection 9 remains the fastest proven maximum-CRF option.

Trim injection 19’s gradient to four minutes while preserving its successful slope and starting composition. All peaks should still elute during the gradient, targeting maximum CRF with its stronger resolution margins in a shorter programmed method.

Test the compact method from injection 23 one temperature step cooler to strengthen early-pair separation while retaining sufficient middle-pair resolution. Injection 6 supports this slope and temperature combination, so maximum CRF is expected with all peaks still inside the shortened gradient.

Use a slightly shallower slope than injection 9 to improve the marginal middle-pair resolution while keeping elution close to its 3.40-minute result. Maximum CRF is already secured; this final run targets a better resolution margin with only a small time cost.
